Read the readiness ledger, confirm it cites archived fresh-VM install evidence with a resolvable path, and verify the cited artifact's hash from the host.

Enumerate the external prerequisites - Apple Developer, Azure Trusted Signing, the Linux signing keypair, the update-feed host, the cloud Mac and the live-eval API keys - and confirm each has a checklist row, an EXT-* mapping and a named owner action.
Confirm the key inventory and the escrow and rotation policy are recorded, and record any prerequisite missing any of those parts.
Confirm an external security audit or penetration test engagement is scheduled and that its report is archived, and verify the archived report's hash from the host.
Record every prerequisite and every cited archive that is absent, with the exact owner action needed to obtain it.

external_oracles.description: The host tree and history search output is the record that no signing secret is committed; absence is proven by the search rather than asserted.
Each cited archived artifact is resolved and hashed by the host, and the hash is compared with the one the ledger records.
The signer and verifier status of every release descriptor is read from the descriptor file itself.
Each named external prerequisite is matched to its checklist row, EXT-* mapping and owner action, and any missing part is recorded by name.

recovery_cases.description: Any committed signing secret fails the run immediately, is reported as a security defect, and its value is never quoted in the evidence.
A cited archive that does not resolve, or whose hash differs from the ledger, is recorded as a stale citation and never accepted.
An external prerequisite that is absent is recorded blocked with the exact owner action required, never as passed or skipped.
A ledger citation pointing at evidence from a different candidate revision is recorded as stale and not counted.
If no external security audit engagement is scheduled or no report is archived, the row is recorded blocked with the exact owner action and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: No signing secret, private key, keychain entry, API key or credential is captured, copied or named beyond its checklist row label; the history search records only whether a match was found and where. Capture the descriptor statuses, the checklist inventory, the resolved archive paths and their hashes. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Start from a clean product profile on the disposable clone with a host per-process network capture running; record from the host the free disk, installed memory, accelerator and architecture of the machine and a listing with hashes of the directory the product uses for model storage.

Open the managed model setup surface and enumerate every catalog entry it offers, recording for each the source it names, the declared size, the declared digest or provenance record, and whether that source is the approved catalog.

Before selecting anything, record the hardware-fit report the product states for each candidate: disk, memory, accelerator, architecture and platform, and which entries it marks as not fitting this machine.

Select an entry the report marks as not fitting and attempt acquisition; record the fail-closed refusal and the recovery it states, and confirm from the host that no byte was written to the model storage directory.
Select a fitting entry, record the explicit download consent the product presents before any transfer, decline it once, and confirm from the capture that no transfer began.

Accept consent, let the transfer run, interrupt it by taking the host network down mid-transfer, then restore the network and resume; record whether the transfer resumed from its recorded position or restarted from the beginning.

On completion, record the size and digest or provenance verification the product performed and the promotion it reports, and confirm from the host that the model became usable at its final path in one step with no partially written artifact left behind.

From the host, replace a second downloaded artifact before promotion with one whose digest does not match its catalog entry, attempt the import, and record the quarantine or deletion the product performs.
Import a model from a local host path outside the catalog, record the provenance the product attributes to it, and confirm it is not presented as catalog-verified.
Disconnect the catalog source entirely, reopen the surface, and record the truthful unavailable state; confirm no cached entry is presented as currently available.
Compare the final model storage listing and hashes against the step-1 baseline and against the digests the catalog declared.

external_oracles.description: A host SHA-256 of each promoted artifact equals the digest its catalog entry declared and the digest the product reported; an artifact the product promoted whose host digest differs fails the run.
The host per-process capture and the model storage listing show no transfer and no written byte before consent was accepted, none for the declined consent, and none for the refused hardware-fit case.
Host directory listings taken during and after promotion show the final path appearing complete, with no partial or temporary artifact surviving success or quarantine.
A host disk, memory, accelerator and architecture inventory taken independently of the product agrees field by field with the hardware-fit report the product stated.
After the digest mismatch a host listing shows the rejected artifact absent from the usable model path and present only in the quarantine location the product named.

recovery_cases.description: Acquisition on a machine that does not meet the stated requirement fails closed with actionable recovery before any transfer; a download that proceeds and exhausts host disk fails the run.
A transfer interrupted mid-flight resumes from its recorded position or restarts explicitly; a resumed transfer whose artifact does not verify against the declared digest fails the run.
An artifact whose size, digest or provenance does not match is quarantined or deleted and never promoted; promotion of a mismatching artifact fails the run and is recorded as a security defect.
With the catalog source unreachable the surface reports a truthful unavailable state; a stale cached entry presented as currently available fails the run.

If no approved catalog source or reference model artifact is available on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed on a substituted artifact.

If the managed acquisition, download-consent or hardware-fit surface the requirement names is absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing control named and is never recorded as passed or skipped.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the catalog inventory, the hardware-fit report, the consent prompts, the transfer and verification records, the quarantine listing and the model storage listings with hashes. Model artifacts themselves are never copied into evidence; only their paths, sizes and digests. The network capture retains connection metadata with payloads discarded at capture time. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Record the host process listing, the host listening-port inventory and the model storage listing with hashes, then launch the packaged product on the disposable clone.

Start the managed local runtime from the product, record the process it claims to supervise, and confirm from the host process listing which process it actually started, under which working directory and with which declared scope.
Cancel a model load while it is in progress and confirm from the host that the runtime process and every child it started are gone and that no partially written artifact remains.

Kill the managed runtime process from the host, record the crash the product reports and the delay before each restart attempt, and confirm the restarts stop at a stated ceiling rather than looping without bound.

Restart the product itself while the runtime is running and record the state it reconstructs: which runtime it reattached to or restarted, and whether the selected route is reported truthfully rather than assumed healthy.
Occupy the runtime's port from a host process, start the runtime again, and record the port-collision state and the recovery the product offers.
Upgrade the managed runtime to a second ratified version, confirm from the host which binary is running afterwards, and confirm the previous version's process is gone.
Corrupt a promoted model artifact from the host and start the runtime against it; record the refusal and confirm no route is presented as healthy.
Uninstall the managed runtime and the model through the product, then compare the host process listing, the listening-port inventory and the storage listing against the step-1 baseline.
Force-close the product while the runtime is running, then read the host process listing and record every runtime or child process that survived.

external_oracles.description: The host process listing taken before, during and after each step is the record of which runtime processes existed; a process the product reported as stopped that the host still lists fails the run.
The host listening-port inventory shows the runtime's port bound only while the product reported the runtime running, and released after stop and after uninstall.
After the force close and after the uninstall, the host process listing contains no runtime or child process attributable to the product.
The host storage listing and hashes after uninstall match the recorded baseline except for exactly what the product stated it retained.
Host clock timestamps of the observed restart attempts show a bounded, increasing delay and a stated ceiling rather than an unbounded restart loop.

recovery_cases.description: A cancelled model load leaves no running process and no partial artifact; a cancellation the host cannot confirm fails the run.
A killed runtime is reported as crashed and restarted under a bounded backoff with a stated ceiling; an unbounded restart loop fails the run.
A port already in use produces a named collision state and an offered recovery, never a silent bind to a different port presented as the same route.
A corrupt model artifact is refused and the route reports unavailable; a route presented as healthy over a corrupt artifact fails the run.
If the ratified managed runtime binary or a model artifact cannot be provisioned on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

If the managed runtime lifecycle controls the requirement names - cancel, restart, upgrade, uninstall - are absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing control named.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the host process listings, the listening-port inventories, the restart timestamps, the reported lifecycle states and the storage listings with hashes. Model artifacts are recorded by path, size and digest only. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone, open the Canvas, and record from the host the path and bytes of the Canvas arrangement metadata file.

Enumerate the fixed regions the Canvas presents and record whether a labeled visual group affordance, a graph-scope indicator and a navigator or minimap region are present; record by name any of the three that is absent.
Create a labeled group over three cards, name it, and confirm the label and the membership are displayed and are written to the arrangement metadata the host can read.
Move one member card out of the group's bounds and one non-member card into them; record how membership changes and confirm the metadata follows.

Pan and zoom to the extremes of the current node set and confirm at each step that the navigator or minimap viewport indicator and the graph-scope indicator stay coherent with the node set actually visible.
Add a node and remove a node, and confirm the group membership, the navigator extent and the graph-scope indicator all update to the new node set.
Enable derived relationship edges as the accepted Canvas contract permits, and record for each derived edge its provenance, its freshness state and how it is distinguished from a person-drawn edge.
Select one derived edge, inspect it, and record the source it attributes the relationship to as a repository path and location a host shell can open.
From a host shell, edit that source so the relationship no longer holds; record the invalidation or stale state the Canvas reports and confirm it does not keep presenting the edge as current.
Re-run the derivation and confirm the edge is removed or re-derived with a new freshness record; confirm from the metadata that no derived edge was ever stored as a person-drawn claim.
Close and relaunch the product; confirm the groups, the graph scope, the navigator state and the derived-edge provenance are restored, and compare the metadata read from the host before and after.

external_oracles.description: A host read of the Canvas arrangement metadata shows the group, its label and its exact membership at each step, equal to what the Canvas displayed.

Every derived edge in the host-readable metadata carries an explicit derived origin, a source location and a freshness record, and is distinguishable from a person-drawn edge; a derived edge stored as a person-drawn claim fails the run.

The repository path and location a derived edge attributes the relationship to can be opened by a host shell and contains the relationship claimed; an attribution the host cannot resolve fails the run.
After the host edit, the host-read metadata marks the affected edge stale, invalidated or removed; metadata that still marks it current fails the run.

A platform accessibility tree dump of the Canvas names a distinct element for the group, the graph-scope indicator and the navigator region, so their presence is proven outside the product's own rendering claim.

recovery_cases.description: If the labeled group affordance, the graph-scope indicator or the navigator region is absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing affordance named and is never recorded as passed or skipped.

If the accepted Canvas contract does not enable derived relationship edges on this build, the derived-edge legs are recorded blocked with the exact contract prerequisite named, never passed and never silently omitted.
A derived edge that survives a change to its attributed source without a stale or invalidation state fails the run and is recorded as a defect against provenance.
Group, scope, navigator or provenance state lost across restart is recorded field by field against the persisted metadata rather than described as a cosmetic variance.

Make the arrangement metadata file read-only from the host and repeat one grouping operation; the failure is reported, the previous arrangement survives, and no derived edge is written as a person-drawn claim.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the Canvas arrangement metadata before and after each step, the derived-edge provenance and freshness records, the accessibility tree dump filtered to the Legion window subtree and the window captures. Window captures are reviewed for incidental on-screen content from other applications before retention. The workspace is a disposable clone containing only synthetic content. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Start from a clean product profile on the disposable clone and record from the host the path and bytes of every store the product uses for Assist session history.
Create an Assist session, exchange several turns that produce at least one proposal, and record the session identifier and the proposal identifier the product displays.
Create a second session, rename it, and confirm both sessions are listed with their names and their most recent activity.
Close and relaunch the product, resume the first session, and confirm its turn history is intact and its proposal link still resolves to the same proposal.
Read the session store from the host and confirm it contains no credential, no provider key and no raw context outside the approved context manifest for those turns.
Export one session through the export control to a host path, inspect every byte of the export, and compare it against what the session displayed.
Delete the second session, confirm it disappears from the list, and confirm from the host that its stored turns are gone while the first session's turns are intact.

Kill the product process from the host mid-turn, relaunch, and record the state of the interrupted session: what was persisted, what was discarded, and whether the product claims a turn completed that it did not.
Make the session store read-only from the host, start a new session, and record the reported failure and the preservation of the existing sessions.
Restore write access, relaunch, and confirm every session, name and proposal link is still correct.

external_oracles.description: A host read of the session store after each step is the record of what persisted; a session the product listed that the store does not contain, or a turn the store contains that the product did not show, fails the run.
A host search of the session store, logs, diagnostics and any support bundle finds no provider credential and no raw context outside the approved context manifest for those turns.
A host byte-level inspection of the export finds exactly the turns the session displayed and no secret-shaped string or unredacted absolute path.
After the delete, a host listing and search of the store shows the deleted session's turns absent and the retained session's turns intact.
The proposal record the resumed session links to is read from the host after restart and is the same proposal, by identifier and content, that the session created before restart.

recovery_cases.description: A turn interrupted by the process being killed is reported truthfully after relaunch; a partially completed turn presented as complete fails the run.
With the session store read-only the failure is reported with the exact OS error, the existing sessions remain readable, and a retry after restoring write access succeeds.
An export found to contain a credential or raw context outside the approved manifest is destroyed and the run is recorded as failed.
A delete that leaves stored turns behind on the host fails the run, with the residual paths named.

If any of the create, resume, rename, delete or export controls the requirement names is absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing control named and is never recorded as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strict policy. Capture the session store bytes, the session and proposal identifiers, the export payload and the store listings. Every export is inspected byte by byte before retention; one found to contain a credential or unapproved raw context is destroyed and the run recorded as failed. Provider credentials are run-scoped and are never captured, copied or named. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Record host SHA-256 values for every file in the disposable clone and the host path of the Delegate checkpoint store, then launch the packaged product on the clone.
Start a Delegate task scoped to a named subtree that will take several turns and will produce at least two proposals.
Let the first turn complete and record the checkpoint the product writes: which turns it marks completed and which proposal effects it records as already applied.
Interrupt the run by killing the product process from the host in the middle of the next turn.
Relaunch and resume the task; record which turns the product re-executes and which it treats as already completed.
Confirm from the workspace hashes and the proposal record that no proposal effect was applied twice and that no completed turn's effect was lost.
Interrupt the run again by making the configured provider route unreachable mid-turn; record the truthful interruption state and resume once the route returns.
Complete the task and compare the final workspace state and proposal history against the recorded turn sequence.
Delete the checkpoint store from the host, relaunch, and confirm the product reports the task as unresumable rather than silently starting over or claiming it finished.
Make the checkpoint store read-only and start a new task; record whether the product refuses to proceed or proceeds without a durable checkpoint.

external_oracles.description: Host SHA-256 values across the workspace show each approved proposal's effect present exactly once; a file changed twice by the same proposal, or a completed turn's effect missing, fails the run.

A host read of the checkpoint store before and after the interruption is the record of which turns were durably marked complete; a turn the product skipped on resume that the store does not mark complete fails the run.
The host-readable proposal record shows each proposal applied exactly once, with its approval preceding its effect.
The host per-process network capture shows no provider request for any turn the product treated as already completed on resume.
The host process listing confirms the product process was killed rather than shut down cleanly, so the resume path being tested is the interruption path.

recovery_cases.description: Any proposal effect applied twice after a resume fails the run and is recorded as a defect, with the duplicated paths and hashes named.
A completed turn whose effect is absent after resume fails the run; the checkpoint contents and the workspace hashes are retained as the evidence of the loss.
With the checkpoint store deleted the task is reported unresumable; a silent restart presented as a resume, or a claim that the task completed, fails the run.
With the checkpoint store read-only the product either refuses to proceed or states plainly that it is running without a durable checkpoint; proceeding while claiming durability fails the run.
If no provider route or credential is available on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed on a recorded fixture.
If the Delegate checkpoint or resume control the requirement names is absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing control named.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the workspace hashes before and after every turn, the checkpoint store contents, the proposal record, the reported interruption states and the network capture as connection metadata with payloads discarded at capture time. The workspace is a disposable clone containing only synthetic content. Provider credentials are run-scoped and are never captured or named. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Build the ratified storage-exercising extension from its source on the host, record its SHA-256 and signature, and record the host path of every storage location the extension host declares.
Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone, install the extension, and record the structured permission list presented at install.
Write a distinct value into workspace scope, into global scope and into secret scope from the extension, and record what the product reports for each.
Read the declared locations from the host: confirm the workspace and global values are present at their declared namespaced paths and that the secret value appears in no product-written file.
Confirm the secret is held through the OS-backed store by showing the entry with a host keyring tool under the extension's namespace.
Open a second workspace and confirm the workspace-scoped value is absent there while the global value is present; install a second extension and confirm neither namespace is readable by it.
Drive the extension past its declared storage quota and confirm the ceiling is enforced with the quota named rather than exceeded.
Restart the product and confirm all three scopes persist with the same values.
Update the extension to a version declaring a storage migration, run it, and record the migrated values and the retention and redaction policy the product states for them.
Uninstall the extension and confirm from the host that its workspace and global namespaces are deleted and its keyring entry removed.
Search every product-written file, log, diagnostic and support bundle from the host for the secret value and confirm no match at any point in the run.

external_oracles.description: A host read of the declared storage locations shows each value only under its own scope and its own extension namespace; a value readable from another scope or another extension fails the run.
A host search for the secret value across every product-written file, log, diagnostic and support bundle returns no match at any point in the run.
A host keyring tool shows the secret entry created under the extension namespace and removed on uninstall, matching the lifecycle the product reported.
A host measurement of the storage location shows it stopped growing at the declared quota; storage beyond the declared ceiling fails the run.
A host listing after uninstall shows the extension's namespaces absent and the rest of the storage location unchanged from the recorded baseline.

recovery_cases.description: A namespace readable by a second extension or by another workspace fails the run and is recorded as a security defect, with the exact path named.
Storage driven past the declared quota is stopped at the ceiling with the quota named, not allowed to continue.
A failed migration preserves the pre-migration values and reports the failure; a migration that discards values without a stated retention decision fails the run.
Any namespace or keyring entry surviving uninstall fails the run, with the residual path or entry named.

If the workspace, global or secret storage scope the requirement names is absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing scope named and is never recorded as passed or skipped.
If no OS keyring provider or signing material is available on this configuration, that leg is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed on a file-backed substitute.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The secret used is a run-scoped test value that is removed at the end of the run; its value is never captured, copied or quoted, and the host search for it records only whether a match was found and where. Capture the permission list, the storage path listings, the keyring entry labels, the quota measurements and the migration records. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Record the host process listing; obtain the two ratified extensions - one declaring the Tier 1 Node-host subset and one declaring the Tier 2 web-worker subset - and record each artifact's SHA-256 and signature.
Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone, install both through the extension surface, and record the API version each declares and the negotiation result the product reports for each.

Trigger the Tier 1 extension's declared activation event and confirm from the host process listing that a supervised host process was started, under which scope and working directory, and that it is the process the product claims to supervise.
Trigger the Tier 2 extension's activation and confirm from the host process listing that it runs in the declared web-worker host with no additional interpreter process started for it.
Exercise every ratified Tier 1 and Tier 2 API and contribution the two extensions declare, and record the observable effect of each in the product.

Call an API outside the supported subset and record the unsupported-API diagnostic the product emits, then confirm from the host that the call produced no filesystem, process or network effect at all.
Install an extension declaring an API version outside the negotiated range and record the refusal, with the host showing no host process started for it.
Drive one host call past its declared bound and confirm the bound is enforced rather than exceeded.
Write and read a value through the storage bridge and confirm it at the declared host path.
Kill the Tier 1 host process from the host, record the recovery the product performs, and confirm the product itself survived by comparing its process identity before and after.
Disable and then uninstall both extensions, and confirm from the host process listing and the extension directory that no host process and no contribution survive.

external_oracles.description: The host process listing is the record of which extension host processes existed, under which scope and parentage; a host process the product did not declare, or a declared one the host cannot see, fails the run.
During and after the Tier 2 activation the host process listing shows no interpreter process beyond the declared web-worker host.

For every call outside the supported subset, host observation of the filesystem, the process table and the network capture shows no effect at all; a call that silently produced a host-observable effect fails the run.
A host read of the declared storage path contains exactly the value written through the bridge and nothing the extension did not write.
After the kill, the disable and the uninstall, the host process listing contains no extension host process attributable to the product.

recovery_cases.description: An extension declaring an API version outside the negotiated range is refused before any host process starts; an activation that proceeds fails the run.
A killed host process is recovered or quarantined with the product still running and the extension's state reported truthfully; a product that exits with its extension host fails the run.
A host call driven past its declared bound is stopped at the ceiling with the bound named, not allowed to continue.
An unsupported API that fails silently, or that appears to succeed, fails the run; the diagnostic must name the API and the host must show no effect.

If the supervised Node or web-worker extension host the requirement names is absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing runtime named and is never recorded as passed or skipped.

If a ratified Tier 1 or Tier 2 extension artifact or its signing material cannot be produced on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed on an unsigned substitute.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strict policy. Capture the artifact hashes and signatures, the negotiation records, the host process listings, the unsupported-API diagnostics, the bound-enforcement records and the storage bridge reads. No signing private key is captured or named; only the verifier's printed subject. The workspace is a disposable clone containing only synthetic content. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Build the ratified webview extension and the hostile webview fixture from their sources on the host, record each artifact's SHA-256 and signature, and start a host per-process network capture.

Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone, install the extension, open its webview, and record the origin, the permitted resource roots and the content security policy the product states for it.

Request from the fixture a resource outside the declared roots and confirm the refusal; confirm from the host file access record and the network capture that nothing outside the roots was read or fetched.

Send a message from the webview to the host that the declared permission set allows and record its observable effect; then send one the permission set does not allow and record the denial and the audit row.
Drive the message channel past its declared quota and confirm the ceiling is enforced with the quota named.
Attempt a workspace change from the webview and confirm it arrives as a proposal requiring approval rather than a direct write.
Run the hostile fixture's attempts at ambient filesystem, network, process and direct storage access in turn, and confirm each is contained and denied with an audit row recording the attempt.
Force the webview to crash and confirm the product survives with the same process identity, then reload the webview and record the lifecycle recovery state.
Close and reopen the webview and confirm no state the permission set forbids persisted across the reopen.
Uninstall the extension and compare the host file inventory, process listing and network capture against the recorded baseline.

external_oracles.description: Host file-access observation and the per-process network capture show no read or fetch outside the declared resource roots at any point; one such access fails the run as a security defect.
Host observation of the filesystem, the process table and the network capture shows no write, spawn or connection attributable to the hostile webview fixture.
Host SHA-256 values show no workspace file changed from a webview request until the resulting proposal was approved.
Each denied message produced no effect the host can observe: no written byte, no spawned process and no connection in the capture.
The host process listing shows the product process alive with the same identity before and after the webview crash.

recovery_cases.description: A resource load, message or capability that escapes the declared origin, roots, policy or permission set fails the run and is recorded as a security defect.
The message channel driven past its declared quota is stopped at the ceiling with the quota named, not allowed to continue.
A crashing webview is recovered or quarantined with the product still running and its lifecycle state reported truthfully.
If the bounded webview UI channel the requirement names is absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing runtime named and is never recorded as passed or skipped.
If the ratified webview extension or the hostile fixture cannot be produced on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed on a substitute.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strict policy. Capture the artifact hashes, the stated origin, roots and policy, the permission set, the audit rows for every contained attempt, the quota records and the host file, process and network inventories. The hostile fixture operates only on synthetic paths created for the run and against a host-controlled endpoint. The network capture retains connection metadata with payloads discarded at capture time. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Record host SHA-256 values for the ratified notebook fixture document and the host process listing, then launch the packaged product on the disposable clone and install the ratified notebook extension.
Open the notebook document and record the document identity the product reports and the identity it assigns each cell; compare both with the document as the host reads it from disk.
Edit one cell, save, and confirm from the host that the saved bytes are a well-formed notebook document whose other cells are unchanged.
Run a cell and confirm from the host process listing that the kernel executed as a bounded child under the product's task or terminal authority; record its output and its exit state.
Interrupt a long-running cell and confirm from the host process listing that the kernel process and its children are gone and no orphan remains.
Restart the kernel and confirm the execution state the product reports matches the new process identity in the host listing.
Make an unsaved cell edit, kill the product process from the host, relaunch, and record the dirty recovery: what was recovered, what was lost, and whether the on-disk document was left corrupt.
Have the extension request a change to the notebook document and confirm it arrives as a proposal requiring approval rather than a direct write.
Change the document on disk from a host shell while it is open and dirty, then save from the product, and record the conflict outcome; confirm both versions survive on refusal.
Close the document, reopen it, and compare the host hashes against the recorded sequence of saves.

external_oracles.description: Host SHA-256 and a host parse of the saved document show a well-formed notebook whose changed cell matches what was edited and whose other cells are byte-identical to the previous save.

The host process listing is the record of the kernel process: its identity, its parentage under the product's task authority and its exit; a cell the product reported as executed with no corresponding process fails the run.
After each interrupt, restart and close, the host process listing contains no kernel process or child attributable to the product.
Host hashes show the document unchanged from an extension request until the resulting proposal was approved.
After the refused save, a host read finds both the on-disk version written from the shell and the product's recovery copy of the dirty version; either one missing fails the run.

recovery_cases.description: A kernel process or child surviving an interrupt or a close fails the run, with its process identity and command line named.
After the kill, unsaved cell content is recovered or its loss is reported explicitly; a corrupt on-disk document, or a silent loss presented as a clean start, fails the run.
A save over a document changed on disk is refused or resolved explicitly with both versions preserved; a silent overwrite fails the run.

If the notebook document and cell surface the requirement names is absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing runtime named and is never recorded as passed or skipped.
If no ratified kernel or its toolchain can be provisioned on this configuration, the execution legs are recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed on a simulated result.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the notebook document hashes before and after every save, the reported document and cell identities, the kernel process listings, the cell outputs and exit states, the recovery copies and the conflict records. The fixture notebook contains only synthetic content. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Record host SHA-256 values for the ratified custom-editor fixture document, then launch the packaged product on the disposable clone and install the ratified custom-editor extension.

Open the document in the custom editor and record the document identity the product reports; open the same path in the ordinary editor and confirm the product reports one document rather than two independently editable copies.
Edit through the custom editor, confirm the dirty state is shown, and confirm from the host that nothing has been written to disk yet.
Save and confirm from the host that the bytes on disk are exactly what the custom editor displayed.
Edit again and revert; confirm from the host that the file returned to its last saved bytes.
Make an unsaved edit and record the backup the product writes at the host path it declares, then read that backup from the host and compare it with the unsaved content.

Confirm from the host that the token is held through the OS-backed store and that no token value appears in any product-written configuration file, log, diagnostic or support bundle.
Let the access token expire, confirm the refresh happens, and confirm the provider recorded it.
Present a response with a mismatched state and then one with a mismatched nonce, and confirm each is rejected with no session established.

Present a token signed by an untrusted key, one with the wrong audience, one with the wrong issuer and one outside its validity window; confirm each is rejected and that no session is established for any of them.
Revoke the session at the provider and confirm the product loses access at its next authenticated operation and reports the revocation.
Take the provider offline and confirm the product reports a truthful unavailable state with recovery offered rather than proceeding as signed in.
Sign out and confirm from the provider's log and the OS-backed store that the session and its token are gone.

external_oracles.description: The identity provider's own log is the record of which sessions were established, refreshed and revoked; a session the product claimed that the provider did not record fails the run.
A host search for the token value across every product-written configuration file, log, diagnostic and support bundle returns no match at any point in the run.
A host keyring tool shows the token reference created at sign-in and removed at sign-out, matching the lifecycle the product reported.
For every invalid response and token, the provider log and the product's own authenticated operations show that no session was established.
The host per-process capture shows connections only to the ratified issuer's endpoints during sign-in, refresh and sign-out.

recovery_cases.description: A token with an untrusted signature, wrong audience, wrong issuer or expired validity that establishes a session fails the run and is recorded as a security defect.
A response with a mismatched state or nonce that is accepted fails the run as a security defect.
After revocation at the provider the next authenticated operation fails and the revocation is reported; continued access fails the run.
With the provider offline the product reports a truthful unavailable state; continuing as signed in fails the run.

If no ratified identity provider endpoint or test account is available on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite named; a stubbed issuer is never accepted as evidence and the run is never recorded as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The account is a run-scoped test account whose session is revoked at the end of the run. No token, client secret or private key value is captured, copied or quoted; the host search for them records only whether a match was found and where. Capture the provider log excerpts for this run only, the request metadata with state and nonce values reduced to their comparison outcome, the keyring entry labels and the network capture as connection metadata with payloads discarded at capture time. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Deploy the collaboration service on a host separate from the product, record the SCIM endpoint it exposes and the tenant credential that will be used, and record the tenant's user and group records in the service store.
From an independent host client, create a user and a group through the SCIM endpoint and record the responses and the identifiers assigned.
Read the service store from the host and confirm the user and the group exist under exactly one tenant.
Repeat the identical create request and confirm the operation is idempotent: the store still holds one user and the response reports the existing resource rather than a duplicate.
Read, replace, patch and then delete the user through the endpoint, confirming each effect in the store after each call.
Exercise the declared filter and pagination parameters and confirm the result sets and page boundaries match what the store holds.
Exceed the declared limits and confirm the stated limit response rather than an unbounded result.
Call the endpoint with no credential and then with a credential belonging to another tenant, and confirm both are refused with the store unchanged.
Provision a user, sign a packaged product instance in as that user, then revoke the user through SCIM and confirm that instance loses access at its next authenticated operation.
Compare the tenant's final user and group set in the store with the recorded sequence of SCIM operations.

external_oracles.description: The service's durable store, read by a host tool, is the record of the tenant's users and groups; a resource the SCIM response reported that the store does not hold fails the run.
The responses observed by an independent host client, not by the product, are the record of the endpoint's behavior for every call.
After the cross-tenant call the store is byte-identical to its state before it, and no resource of the other tenant is visible in any response.
After the repeated create the store holds exactly one resource; a second resource fails the run.
After the SCIM revocation the running product instance's next authenticated operation fails, observed from the service log rather than from the product's own claim.

recovery_cases.description: A repeated create producing a second resource fails the run and is recorded as an idempotency defect.
A call authenticated for one tenant that reads or changes another tenant's resources fails the run and is recorded as a security defect.
An unauthenticated call that succeeds fails the run as a security defect; the store must be unchanged.
A request beyond the declared limits that returns an unbounded result fails the run, with the declared limit and the observed result size recorded.

If no deployable collaboration service artifact, service endpoint, tenant credential or identity provider is available on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite named; an in-process runtime, a loopback stub or a fixture harness is never substituted for the service and the run is never recorded as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The tenant credential is run-scoped and revoked at the end of the run; its value is never captured or named. Capture the SCIM request and response metadata, the service store reads and the service log excerpts for this run only. User and group identifiers, display names and addresses are synthetic and run-local. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Take the signed service package from the release artifact set, record its SHA-256, verify its signature with the platform verifier, and record the SBOM and provenance artifacts shipped with it.
Record the desktop product version the package's compatibility manifest pins and confirm it matches the packaged product under test.
Install the service on a clean host from the package alone, and record every path it created and every service registration and listening port it made.
Apply the documented production configuration, confirm the service validates it, then present a configuration the package declares insecure and confirm the service refuses to start on it.
Start the service, run its migrations, and confirm from the store that the schema is at the expected version.
Query the health and readiness endpoints from the host and compare their answers with the service's actual process and store state.
Connect the packaged product to the service and complete one shared-workspace operation end to end.
Take a backup with the documented procedure, upgrade to the next package version, run its migrations, and confirm the data and the desktop compatibility pin after the upgrade.
Roll back to the previous version using the documented procedure and the backup, and confirm the restored data and schema version.
Interrupt an upgrade mid-way by killing the process, restart, and record the recovery the documented procedure produces.
Uninstall and compare the host filesystem, the service registrations and the listening-port inventory against the clean baseline.

external_oracles.description: The platform signature verifier's exact output for the service package is retained; an unsigned or untrusted package that installs fails the run.
A host tool compares the shipped SBOM against the files the installation actually placed on the host; a component present on disk and absent from the SBOM fails the run.
The host filesystem, service registration and listening-port inventories before install and after uninstall are compared; every difference is named.
A host read of the store reports the schema version after each migration, upgrade and rollback, matching what the documented procedure states.
The health and readiness endpoints queried directly from the host agree with the service's actual process and store state at the same moment.

recovery_cases.description: A configuration the package declares insecure that the service starts on fails the run and is recorded as a security defect.
A failed migration leaves the previous schema and data intact and reports the failure; a partially migrated store fails the run.
An upgrade interrupted mid-way recovers to a working version through the documented procedure; a host left with no working service fails the run.
A rollback that loses data the backup contained fails the run, with the backup and the restored store both retained.
A service version accepted against a desktop product version outside its compatibility pin fails the run.

If no signed service package, clean host or signing verifier is available on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite named and is never recorded as passed on an unsigned build or a shared host.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the package hash and verifier output, the SBOM and provenance artifacts, the install and uninstall inventories, the configuration files with secret values redacted, the migration and health output and the backup and restore command output. No signing private key or production credential is captured or named. The clean host holds only run-local synthetic data. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Start from a clean product profile on the disposable clone, record the consent state files from the host, and produce a small set of training candidates through ordinary consented work; record their identifiers and the host path of the candidate store.
Open the candidate feedback surface as an authorized user and confirm every candidate it lists carries its consent state, its provenance and its redaction result.
Confirm the surface refuses to show or act on a candidate whose consent was never granted, and confirm from the store that no such candidate is present.
Accept one candidate and confirm from the store that its downstream corpus eligibility changed exactly as displayed.
Reject a second candidate and confirm from the store that it is marked ineligible while remaining attributable to its source.
Correct a third candidate, read the corrected content from the host byte by byte, and confirm the correction preserved the redaction policy and reintroduced no secret and no unapproved raw context.
Withdraw a fourth candidate and confirm from the store that it is no longer eligible and that its provenance record survives for audit.
Delete a fifth candidate and confirm from the host that its stored content is gone, that a deletion receipt exists, and that the corpus no longer counts it.
Attempt each of the six operations as an unauthorized user and confirm each is refused with the store unchanged.
Restart the product and confirm every state above survived, then export the eligible corpus and confirm it contains exactly the candidates the operations left eligible.

external_oracles.description: A host read of the candidate store after each operation is the record of consent, provenance, redaction and eligibility; a state the product displayed that the store does not hold fails the run.
The exported corpus read from a host path contains exactly the candidates the operations left eligible, and no withdrawn, rejected or deleted candidate.
After the delete, a host listing shows the stored content absent and the receipt identifier matching what the product displayed.
A host byte-level inspection of the corrected candidate and of the exported corpus finds no secret-shaped string and no raw context outside the approved redaction policy.
The candidate store is byte-identical before and after every operation attempted as an unauthorized user.

recovery_cases.description: An operation performed by an unauthorized user that changes the store fails the run and is recorded as a security defect.
A candidate shown or acted on without consent fails the run and is recorded as a privacy defect.
A correction or export that reintroduces a secret or unapproved raw context is destroyed and the run is recorded as failed.
A delete that leaves candidate content on the host, or that issues a receipt without removing the content, fails the run with the residual paths named.

If any of the review, accept, reject, correct, withdraw or delete controls the requirement names is absent from the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing control named and is never recorded as passed or skipped.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The candidates are produced from a disposable clone containing only synthetic content. Capture the candidate store reads, the displayed consent, provenance and redaction states, the deletion receipts and the exported corpus. Every corrected candidate and the export are inspected byte by byte before retention; one found to contain a secret or unapproved raw context is destroyed and the run recorded as failed. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate and honour the deletion receipt.

steps: Clone the repository at the candidate revision into a disposable directory and record the revision.
Resolve the published native platform matrix document from a host stat, record its path, and record failed with the path searched if it does not resolve.

Read the platform matrix and record whether it names a finite set of supported Windows, macOS and Linux versions and architectures, reference hardware, display/DPI classes, input and accessibility tools, and the configurations it declares unavailable or blocked; record every one of those eight parts it omits.
Confirm each entry is finite and named rather than open-ended, recording every entry expressed as a range, a wildcard or an unbounded phrase.
Resolve the published distribution matrix document the same way and record its path or record failed with the path searched.

Read the distribution matrix and record whether it names supported OS versions and architectures, package formats, signing and notarization verifiers, release channels, update feeds, offline artifact variants, clean-machine configurations and owner-held external prerequisites; record every one of those nine parts it omits.
Compare both matrices with plans/completion/matrix.json and record every configuration the register uses that neither matrix names, and every matrix entry the register has no configuration for.
Record the SHA-256 of both documents from a host shell so a later edit is detectable.
Confirm each owner-held external prerequisite the distribution matrix names carries an owner action and a current state, and record every one that does not.
Record every claim either matrix makes about a configuration being supported that no evidence run in plans/evidence has ever exercised.

external_oracles.description: A host stat is the record of whether each matrix document exists at the candidate revision; a document that does not resolve is recorded as failed with the exact path searched, never as pending.
The host SHA-256 of each resolved document is recorded, so what was read is fixed and a later edit to the matrix is detectable.

A host comparison between the matrix entries and the configuration ids in plans/completion/matrix.json is the record of coverage in both directions; the matrix is not edited during the run to close a gap.
Each part the requirement names is recorded present or absent by quoting the document, so an omission is evidenced rather than asserted.

recovery_cases.description: A matrix document that does not exist at the candidate revision records the row failed with the exact path searched; it is never recorded as passed, skipped or pending, and the document is not authored during the run.
A matrix that resolves but omits a part the requirement names records failed with that part named; a partially complete matrix is never recorded as passed.
An entry expressed as a range, a wildcard or an unbounded phrase fails the finiteness check and is recorded verbatim.
A configuration the register uses that the matrix does not name is recorded as a divergence with both values; neither file is edited during the run.
If the repository cannot be cloned at the candidate revision on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the resolved document paths, their SHA-256 values, the quoted part inventory and the register cross-check output. Only repository content is in scope; no credential, signing key or owner contact detail is captured, and an owner-held prerequisite is recorded by its checklist label rather than by any secret it refers to. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

Read the build/test/debug matrix and record, for each of the four languages, whether it names project configurations, package and environment discovery, build and task runners, test runners, debug adapters, launch settings, supported versions, OS coverage, and the prerequisite and unavailable states; record every part it omits.

Compare the language servers, formatters, runners and adapters both matrices name with the pinned descriptors the repository actually registers, and record every entry that names a version the repository does not pin and every pinned descriptor neither matrix names.
Record the SHA-256 of both documents and of every fixture archive they name.
Record every supported entry in either matrix for which no configuration exists in plans/completion/matrix.json.

external_oracles.description: A host stat is the record of whether each matrix document exists at the candidate revision; a path that does not resolve is recorded as failed with the exact path searched.
Each fixture identity the language matrix declares is verified by a host SHA-256 of the fixture it names; a hash that differs, or a fixture that does not resolve, is recorded with both values.
A host comparison between the versions the matrices name and the descriptors the repository registers is the record of agreement; neither side is edited during the run.
Each part the requirement names is recorded present or absent per language by quoting the document.

recovery_cases.description: A matrix document that does not exist at the candidate revision records the row failed with the exact path searched and is never authored during the run.
A matrix that omits one of the four required languages, or a part of one, records failed with the language and part named.
A fixture whose host hash differs from the recorded one, or that does not resolve, records failed with both values; the matrix is not updated to match the fixture during the run.
A version the matrix names that the repository does not pin, or a pinned descriptor no matrix names, is recorded as a divergence with both readings.
If the repository cannot be cloned at the candidate revision on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the resolved document paths, the per-language part inventory, the fixture hashes and the pin cross-check output. Only repository content and the fixtures the matrices name are in scope. No registry token or download credential is captured, and command lines are recorded with environment values removed. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

Record the SHA-256 of both documents from a host shell.
Record every named peer implementation or supported API entry for which no acceptance configuration or fixture exists anywhere in the repository.

external_oracles.description: A host stat is the record of whether each contract exists at the candidate revision; a path that does not resolve is recorded as failed with the exact path searched.
The host SHA-256 of each resolved contract is recorded so what was read is fixed.
A host comparison between the versions the contracts name and the versions the repository implements is the record of agreement in both directions; neither side is edited during the run.
Each acceptance configuration the contract declares is looked up in plans/completion/matrix.json and recorded present or absent by id.

recovery_cases.description: A contract that does not exist at the candidate revision records the row failed with the exact path searched; it is never recorded as passed or pending and is not authored during the run.
A contract that resolves but omits a part the requirement names records failed with that part named.
A protocol or API version named but not implemented, or implemented but not named, is recorded with both readings as a divergence.
A declared acceptance configuration with no matching entry in the register is recorded by id as a failed outcome; no configuration is added during the run.
If the repository cannot be cloned at the candidate revision on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the resolved contract paths, their SHA-256 values, the part inventory and the version cross-check output. Only repository content is in scope; no peer credential, token or endpoint secret is captured, and a credential the contract names is recorded by its role label only. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.
