Resolve the ratified SSH and dev-container configuration matrix from a host stat and record its path, or record failed with the path searched.

Read the remote matrix and record whether it names finite host, image, architecture, identity, credential, agent, language, terminal, debug, extension and port-forwarding configurations, each with named versions, prerequisites and external acceptance oracles; record every one of those parts it omits and every entry that is not finite.

Resolve the published collaboration and enterprise identity/policy matrix and record whether it names supported endpoints, roles, transports, retention and executable acceptance oracles; record every part it omits.

Resolve the published telemetry and training matrix and record whether it names supported consent modes, retention and export destinations, training corpus and model/runtime configurations, reproducibility thresholds, and the Manual/offline privacy rules; record every part it omits.

For each external acceptance oracle any of the three matrices names, record whether it reads state from outside the product process and record by name every declared oracle that is the product reporting on itself.
Compare the three matrices with plans/completion/matrix.json and record every declared configuration that has no register configuration and every register configuration none of them names.
Record the SHA-256 of all three documents from a host shell.
Record every prerequisite any of the three matrices names as owner-held together with its current state, and record every one that has no state at all.

external_oracles.description: A host stat is the record of whether each matrix exists at the candidate revision; a path that does not resolve is recorded as failed with the exact path searched.
The host SHA-256 of each resolved matrix is recorded so what was read is fixed.

Each acceptance oracle a matrix declares is classified from its own text as reading state inside or outside the product process; a declared oracle that is the product asserting about itself is recorded by name as a failed outcome.
A host comparison between the declared configurations and plans/completion/matrix.json is the record of coverage in both directions.

recovery_cases.description: A matrix that does not exist at the candidate revision records its row failed with the exact path searched and is not authored during the run.
A matrix that resolves but omits a part its requirement names records failed with that part named.
A declared acceptance oracle that reads only the product's own report is recorded by name as a failed outcome; it is not reclassified during the run.
An owner-held prerequisite with no recorded state is recorded blocked with the exact owner action required, never as passed or skipped.
If the repository cannot be cloned at the candidate revision on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the resolved document paths, their SHA-256 values, the part inventory, the oracle classification and the register cross-check. Only repository content is in scope. No SSH key, host fingerprint, identity-provider secret, collection endpoint credential or telemetry payload is captured; a credential or endpoint a matrix names is recorded by its label only. Redact absolute user-home segments and any host name that is not a documented example. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the repository at the candidate revision into a disposable directory and record the revision.

Resolve each ADR these rows name from a host stat - the ACP host adapter-bridge ADR, the extension-host runtime ADR, the update strategy and manifest-format ADR, and the collaboration operation-layer ADR - and record each path and its SHA-256, or record failed with the exact path searched.
For each resolved ADR record its status, its decision and the surface it decides, and record every ADR whose status is not one that the repository treats as in force.

Read the dependency policy and record whether it admits the runtime the extension-host ADR chooses and whether it cites that ADR; record the exact policy entry or record failed with what the policy says instead.
Read the dependency policy entry the ACP host ADR requires the same way and record it or its absence.
Read the release pipeline configuration and record whether the update strategy and the manifest format it uses are the ones the update ADR documents; record every divergence with both readings.
Read the collaboration operation-layer ADR and record whether it links the chosen reconciliation layer to a collaboration substrate that exists in the repository, resolving both from the host.
Run the deferred-surfaces gate from a host shell against xtask/deferred-surfaces.toml and record its exit status and full output.

For each frozen surface the gate configures, record its readiness-ledger row and, where the row claims anything other than deferred, not started or blocked, record whether the surface's own ADR, policy, test target and product evidence all resolve from the host.

In a scratch copy promote one frozen surface's ledger row to a validated status without adding any of the four artifacts, re-run the gate, record the exit status, then discard the scratch copy and re-run the gate on the unmodified tree.
Record every ADR, policy entry, test target or evidence path any of these rows names that does not resolve, with the exact path searched.

external_oracles.description: A host stat is the record of whether each ADR, policy entry, test target and evidence path exists at the candidate revision; a path that does not resolve is recorded with the exact path searched.
The host SHA-256 of every resolved ADR and policy file is recorded, so what was read is fixed and a later edit is detectable.
The host shell's recorded exit status for each deferred-surfaces run is the record of pass or failure, not any message the tool prints.

With one frozen surface promoted and none of its four artifacts added, the host-recorded gate exit status is non-zero and the output names that surface; a gate that waves the promotion through fails the run.
`git status --porcelain` in the clone is empty after the scratch promotion is discarded, so no injected change survived the run.

recovery_cases.description: An ADR that does not resolve at the candidate revision records its row failed with the exact path searched; the ADR is not authored during the run.

A dependency policy that does not admit the ADR's chosen runtime, or a pipeline configuration that does not use the documented manifest format, is recorded with both readings; neither is edited during the run.
A gate that accepts a promotion with none of the four artifacts present is recorded as a governance defect with the surface named, and the gate is not reconfigured during the run to make it pass.
Any injected promotion surviving in the clone after the run fails the run and the clone is destroyed.
If the gate cannot be built or run on this configuration, that leg is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the resolved ADR, policy, test-target and evidence paths with their SHA-256 values, the gate command lines, exit statuses and bounded output, and the readiness-ledger rows. Only repository content is in scope. Command lines are recorded with environment values removed and only allow-listed variable names retained. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the repository at the candidate revision into a disposable directory and record the revision and the toolchain versions from a host shell.
Enumerate the workloads the perf harness declares and record, for each, whether it exercises a product workload or a synthetic stand-in, quoting the workload definition.

Record whether the 100MB large-file workload is one of the workloads the standard harness run executes, and record by path any script outside the standard run that would have to be invoked separately to exercise it.
Run the standard perf harness from a host shell and record the exact command line, the exit status and the list of workloads it actually executed.
Compare the executed list with the declared list and record every declared workload the standard run skipped and every workload executed that is not declared.
Read the CI configuration and record which job runs the perf harness, on which operating systems, and where each job archives its report.

Record the per-job outcome of the most recent perf-harness run on each of the three operating systems from the CI provider, together with the archived report each job produced, and record by name every operating system with no job at all.
Confirm each CI run archives a trend entry, resolve the trend entries for the recorded runs from the host, and record every run with no trend entry.

In a scratch copy introduce a regression that exceeds a declared budget, run the harness with the strict flag, and record the exit status and the budget the output names; then discard the scratch copy and re-run the harness on the unmodified tree.
Record the SHA-256 of every archived report and trend entry the run resolved.

external_oracles.description: The host shell's recorded exit status for each harness invocation is the record of pass or failure, not any summary the harness prints.

The workloads the standard run actually executed are read from the run's own host-captured output and compared with the declared list, so 'the workload is in the harness' is measured rather than asserted.

The CI provider's own per-job status and artifact listing, read from the host, are the record of which operating systems ran the harness and which reports were archived; no outcome is taken from a summary written by hand.
With an injected regression the host-recorded exit status under the strict flag is non-zero and the output names the exceeded budget; a strict run that passes fails this scenario.
Every archived report and trend entry is resolved and hashed by the host, so the archive is shown to exist rather than cited.

recovery_cases.description: A required product workload reachable only through a side script is recorded failed with that script's path; it is not moved into the harness during the run.
An operating system with no perf-harness job is recorded failed by name; a two-OS result is never recorded as a three-OS pass.
A CI run with no archived trend entry is recorded failed with the run identifier; a trend entry is not backfilled during the run.
A strict run that accepts an injected budget regression is recorded as a gate defect with the injected value and the budget; the budget is not adjusted to make the run fail.
A perf-harness job whose runner is unavailable, or a harness that cannot be built on this configuration, is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed or skipped.
Any injected regression surviving in the clone after the run fails the run and the clone is destroyed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the workload inventory, the harness command lines, exit statuses and bounded output, the CI job identifiers and outcomes, and the archived report and trend-entry paths with their hashes. No CI credential, token or webhook secret is captured, and log excerpts are scanned for token-shaped strings before retention. Measurements are recorded with the host identity reduced to its configuration id. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the repository at the candidate revision into a disposable directory and record the revision.
Read the CI configuration and record which job runs the eval regression gate, what change set it runs on, and what result makes it fail; record failed if no job runs it at all.
Run the bench in recorded mode from a host shell and record the exact command line, the exit status and the per-task results.
Enumerate the bench corpus and record the number of tasks, the number of distinct fixture repositories, and which tasks are held out, comparing each count with the minimum the requirement states.
For each scored task confirm the score came from executing the fixture task rather than from budget arithmetic over a recorded plan, quoting the per-task record that shows which.
Enumerate the hostile fixtures, record each fixture's score, and confirm the run treats a successful exfiltration as a hard failure rather than a lowered score.
In a scratch copy make one hostile fixture succeed at exfiltration, re-run the bench, record the exit status, then discard the scratch copy and re-run on the unmodified tree.
Resolve plans/evidence/production/BENCH/baseline-raw-v1.md from the host, record its SHA-256, and record the task-set hash it states together with the task-set hash the current corpus produces.

Read the CI configuration and record that recorded mode runs on every change and that live mode is opt-in and scheduled rather than triggered by an ordinary change; record every place either statement does not hold.
Record every credential-dependent leg the bench declares, and record for each whether it ran, was recorded blocked with a named missing credential, or was silently skipped.

external_oracles.description: The host shell's recorded exit status for each bench invocation is the record of pass or failure, not any score summary the bench prints.
The workflow file content read from the host is the record of which job runs the eval gate, which mode runs on every change and how live mode is triggered.
The task count, the distinct fixture-repository count and the held-out set are counted from the corpus on disk, not read from a claimed figure.
The archived raw baseline is resolved and hashed by the host and its stated task-set hash is compared with the hash the current corpus produces; a divergence is recorded with both values.
With one hostile fixture made to succeed, the host-recorded exit status is non-zero; a run that records a lowered score and exits zero fails this scenario.

recovery_cases.description: If no CI job runs an eval regression gate on agent or product changes, the row is recorded failed with the workflow files searched; a gate is not added during the run.
A corpus below the stated task or repository minimum, or without a held-out subset, is recorded failed with the measured counts; tasks are not added during the run.
A task scored by budget arithmetic rather than by executing the fixture is recorded by task identifier as a failed outcome.
A successful exfiltration that does not hard-fail the run is recorded as a security defect with the fixture named; the threshold is not adjusted during the run.
A missing raw baseline, or one whose task-set hash differs from the current corpus, is recorded failed with both values; the baseline is never regenerated during the run.
A live leg whose credential is unavailable is recorded blocked with the exact missing credential named and never as passed or silently skipped.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the bench command lines, exit statuses, per-task and per-fixture results, the corpus inventory and the baseline path with its hash. No provider API key or live credential is captured or named beyond its checklist label, and bench output is scanned for token-shaped strings before retention. The hostile fixtures and the injected exfiltration are synthetic and confined to the disposable clone; any captured payload is inspected before retention and destroyed if it contains a real secret. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the repository at the candidate revision into a disposable directory and record the revision.
Search the legion-ui crate from a host shell for state it owns rather than projects and for any write path into workspace or buffer authority, and record every hit with its file and line.
Record for each hit whether it is a projection of state owned elsewhere or an authority the crate holds itself, quoting the code that decides which.
Resolve the headless-input evidence document from a host stat, record its path and SHA-256, and record the revision and the command output it cites.
Re-run the command the evidence document cites from a host shell at the revision it names, and compare the output with the output the document records, recording every difference.
Record whether the revision the evidence document cites is the candidate revision, and record both values when it is not.
Locate the CI gate that forbids egui::TextEdit in the code canvas, record the job that runs it, and run it from a host shell on the unmodified tree recording the exit status.

In a scratch copy reintroduce egui::TextEdit into the code canvas, re-run the gate, record the exit status and confirm the output names the offending file; then discard the scratch copy and re-run the gate.
Locate the 100MB open and scroll test, record whether it is present and whether it is currently ignored, and record the exact attribute or annotation that makes it so.
Record whether the streaming mode the test waits on is implemented at this revision, and record whether the test's ignored state matches that answer.
Run the test with ignored tests included from a host shell and record the exit status and the failure it reports if it fails.
Read from the headless-input evidence document the list of representative workflows it records under the P1.F1.T3 backlog card, and record each entry verbatim together with the count.

For each recorded workflow, search `crates/legion-desktop/tests/headless_input.rs` from a host shell for the test function that drives that workflow through the harness, and record the function name and its line, or record that no such function was found.
Run the headless input harness from a host shell naming each of those test functions, and record the per-test result and the overall exit status.

external_oracles.description: The host search output is the record of every authority-shaped hit in legion-ui and of the presence or absence of egui::TextEdit in the code canvas; absence is proven by the search, not asserted.
The host shell's recorded exit status for each gate and test invocation is the record of pass or failure.

The command the evidence document cites is re-run on the host and its output compared with the recorded output; a difference is recorded with both texts rather than resolved by re-running until they agree.
With egui::TextEdit reintroduced into the code canvas, the host-recorded gate exit status is non-zero and the output names the offending file; a gate that passes fails this scenario.
`git status --porcelain` in the clone is empty after the scratch reintroduction is discarded.

The host search over `crates/legion-desktop/tests/headless_input.rs` and the host shell's per-test result output are the record of which representative workflows are driven through the harness; a workflow the evidence document lists with no matching test function is recorded from the search, never from the document's own claim.

recovery_cases.description: A place where legion-ui owns state or writes authority directly is recorded by file and line as a failed outcome; the code is not changed during the run.

An evidence document that does not resolve, cites no revision or command output, or cites a revision other than the candidate, records the row failed with both readings; the document is not regenerated during the run.
A gate that accepts the reintroduced widget is recorded as a gate defect with the injected file named; the gate pattern is not widened during the run.
A test whose ignored state does not match whether streaming mode is implemented is recorded failed with both readings; the attribute is not flipped during the run.
Any injected widget or attribute surviving in the clone after the run fails the run and the clone is destroyed.
If the toolchain cannot build the gate or the test on this configuration, that leg is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

A representative workflow the evidence document lists for which no headless test function is found, or whose test does not run, records the row failed with the workflow text and the search performed; no test is added and the recorded workflow list is not shortened during the run.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the host search outputs, the gate and test command lines with their exit statuses and bounded output, the evidence document path with its SHA-256, and the re-run comparison. Only repository content is in scope. Redact absolute user-home segments and the toolchain install path. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the repository at the candidate revision into a disposable directory and record the revision.
Enumerate every risk classifier rule and record its identifier, and record every rule whose identifier is generated rather than stable across runs.
For each rule identifier locate the test case that enumerates it and record the test's location, and record by identifier every rule with no enumerated test case.
Run the classifier test suite from a host shell and record the exact command line, the exit status and the per-rule results.
In a scratch copy change one rule's identifier, re-run the suite, and record whether any test failed; then discard the scratch copy and re-run the suite on the unmodified tree.
Enumerate the provider smoke tests and record for each whether it is a recorded or a live test.
Run the recorded smoke tests from a host shell with a per-process network capture running, and record the exit status together with every outbound connection the capture observed.
Read the CI configuration and record which job runs the recorded smoke tests and whether it runs without any provider credential configured.
Read the CI configuration for the live smoke tests and record the exact condition that gates them, then record what the job does when that condition is absent.
Run the live smoke tests from a host shell with no credential present and record whether the result is a named blocked outcome, a failure, or a silent skip.

external_oracles.description: The host shell's recorded exit status for each suite invocation is the record of pass or failure.
Each rule identifier has a recorded present-or-absent enumerated test case and a recorded per-rule suite result, so 'each rule has a test case' is counted rather than asserted.
With one rule identifier changed, at least one test fails on the host; a suite that stays green proves the identifier is not actually enumerated and fails this scenario.
The host per-process network capture is the record of whether the recorded smoke tests reached any external endpoint; an offline claim is proven by the capture, not by the absence of an error.
The workflow file content read from the host is the record of which job runs the recorded suite, whether it runs without credentials, and what condition gates the live suite.

recovery_cases.description: A rule with no enumerated test case, or without a stable identifier, is recorded by identifier as a failed outcome; a test is not added during the run.
A recorded smoke test that opens an outbound connection is recorded as a failed outcome with the observed endpoint; the capture is authoritative over the suite's own claim of being offline.
A live smoke test that reports success or is silently skipped when no credential is present is recorded as a gate defect; a truthful result is a named blocked outcome stating the missing credential.
The live legs themselves are recorded blocked with the exact missing credential named, never as passed or skipped; no substitute endpoint or stub provider is used.
Any changed rule identifier surviving in the clone after the run fails the run and the clone is destroyed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the rule inventory, the per-rule results, the suite command lines and exit statuses, the network capture summary and the workflow excerpts. No provider API key or credential is captured or named beyond its checklist label; captured output and the network summary are scanned for token-shaped strings before retention, and the capture records endpoints and byte counts rather than payload bodies. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the repository at the candidate revision into a disposable directory and record the revision and the trainer toolchain versions from a host shell.

Build a synthetic consented trace set on the host that contains, by construction, granted, denied, missing-consent, expired and revoked entries, and record the identifier and expected disposition of each.
Run the consented corpus export from a host shell and record the exact command line, the exit status and the identifiers of the traces the exported corpus contains.
Compare the exported set with the expected dispositions and record every denied, missing, expired or revoked trace that survived and every granted trace that was dropped.

Inspect the exported corpus byte by byte on the host and record every occurrence of content outside the metadata-only redaction policy and every secret-shaped string the secret scanning should have caught.
Record the source, corpus and dataset fingerprints the export binds, and confirm each resolves to the artifact it names from the host.
Alter one fingerprint in a scratch copy of the exported corpus, present it at the trainer boundary, record whether the boundary rejects it, then discard the scratch copy.

Run the adapter training entrypoint on the ratified model, runtime and hardware configuration and record the code revision, corpus identity, consent state, base model revision, tokenizer, seed, hyperparameters, observed resources and the resulting adapter hash.
Run the held-out comparison and the Legion-Bench comparison and record both results together with the archived comparison the repository already holds, recording every difference.
Repeat the whole trace-to-adapter-to-evaluation chain from the same recorded inputs and record whether the adapter hash and both comparison results reproduce, quoting each pair of values.
Record the independent accept or reject review the run carries, including who performed it and on which recorded values, and record its absence if there is none.
Record the SHA-256 of the exported corpus, the produced adapter and every archived comparison the run resolved.

external_oracles.description: The host shell's recorded exit status for each export, training and comparison invocation is the record of pass or failure, not any summary the pipeline prints.

A host byte inspection of the exported corpus is the record of which traces it contains and whether any content falls outside the metadata-only redaction policy; the exporter's own report never substitutes for it.
Every source, corpus and dataset fingerprint the export binds is resolved and hashed by the host against the artifact it names, and a divergence is recorded with both values.
With one fingerprint altered, the trainer boundary's host-recorded exit status is non-zero and the output names the mismatch; a boundary that accepts the altered corpus fails the run.

The adapter hash and both comparison results from the second chain are compared with the first on the host; any difference is recorded with both values rather than resolved by repeating until they agree.

recovery_cases.description: A denied, missing-consent, expired or revoked trace present in the exported corpus is recorded as a privacy defect with its identifier, the corpus is destroyed, and the run is recorded failed.

Content outside the metadata-only policy, or a secret-shaped string the scanning missed, destroys the corpus and records the run failed with the rule that should have caught it named; the policy is not relaxed during the run.
A trainer boundary that accepts an altered fingerprint is recorded as an integrity defect with both fingerprints; the boundary is not reconfigured during the run.

An adapter hash or comparison result that does not reproduce from the same recorded inputs is recorded failed with both values and the inputs that were held fixed; the seed or hyperparameters are not adjusted to obtain a match.
A training run with no independent accept or reject review, or one reviewed by the same party that produced it, is recorded failed; the review is not performed during the run by the runner.

If the ratified model, runtime or hardware configuration is not available on this host, the training and evaluation legs are recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite named; no smaller model, different runtime, reduced hardware or recorded stand-in is substituted, and the legs are never recorded as passed or skipped.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The traces are synthetic and generated for the run; no real user trace, prompt or source content enters the pipeline. Capture the command lines, exit statuses, the trace dispositions, the fingerprints, the recorded training provenance, the comparison results and the artifact hashes. The exported corpus and the produced adapter are inspected before retention and destroyed if they contain a secret-shaped string or content outside the metadata-only policy; only their hashes and the disposition table are retained. No model weight, adapter binary or corpus body is retained. Redact absolute user-home segments and any accelerator or host serial identity. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Install the pinned candidate build on the machine named by this configuration cell, start from a clean product profile, and record the installed artifact SHA-256 and every consent state file the product writes.

Start a host per-process DNS, TCP and UDP capture over the product process tree and configure a host-controlled collection endpoint as the only telemetry and training destination; record that the endpoint log is empty before any work begins.
Complete first run and record, for each of the crash, product and raw-training consent controls, the state it starts in and the purpose, retention and destination the product displays for it.

Work in a real project with every consent off for the period recorded for this run, then confirm from the capture, the endpoint log and the spool directory that nothing was captured, queued or uploaded.

Grant product and raw-training consent, do ordinary work that produces training candidates, and record for each capture the preview the product shows before upload together with the redaction result it reports.
Read the payloads the host endpoint received and compare each byte for byte with the preview that was shown for it, recording every difference.
Revoke raw-training consent part way through and confirm from the endpoint log and from the spool that no item captured under that consent is uploaded afterwards.

Take the endpoint offline, keep working, then restart the product and confirm from the spool that queued items survived the restart with a truthful pending state and that none was uploaded while consent was revoked.
Restore consent and the endpoint, let the retry drain the spool, and confirm the endpoint received each queued item exactly once.
Export the consented training bundle to a host path through the product's own export route as an authorized user, and record the export path, the manifest it writes and their SHA-256 values.

Run the repository corpus exporter from a host shell against that bundle, running `cargo run -p xtask -- training-corpus --out <run-dir>` with the corpus id, expansion, seed and holdout values recorded for this run, and record its exit status, the emitted `train.jsonl`, `holdout.jsonl` and export manifest, and their SHA-256 values.
Read the exported corpus from the host byte by byte and confirm it carries no trace whose consent was denied, expired or revoked earlier in this run, and no secret-shaped string.

Run the consent-gated adapter training from a host shell with the model revision, tokenizer, hyperparameters, seed and device recorded for this run, passing the export manifest as the consent manifest, and record the exit status, the adapter artifact and its SHA-256.
Run the held-out evaluation against that adapter, the same consent manifest and the holdout split, and record the base-versus-adapter comparison it writes.
Repeat the training run under the reproducibility rule recorded for this run and record whether the adapter hash and metrics fall inside the threshold recorded before the first run.
Revoke consent for one trace already present in the export, re-run the corpus exporter and the trainer against the same run directory, and record whether each refuses the revoked trace or proceeds.

Record the retention the product displayed for each consented bundle and, after the retention window recorded for this run has elapsed, confirm from a host listing that the expired bundle was purged and that a re-run of the exporter no longer emits it.

Delete the remaining consented telemetry and training bundles through the product as an authorized user, record each deletion receipt, and confirm from the host that the stored payload and its key are absent and that a re-run of the exporter no longer emits the deleted rows.
Restart the product once more and record the consent, spool, export, retention and deletion state it reports, comparing each against the host state read directly.

external_oracles.description: The host-controlled collection endpoint's own log is the record of what was uploaded and when: nothing while every consent was off, nothing captured under a revoked consent, and exactly one delivery per queued item after the retry drained.

The host per-process DNS, TCP and UDP capture over the product process tree is the record of every destination the product contacted; the product's own report of its network activity is never accepted in its place.

A host byte comparison of each received payload against the preview shown for it is the record of whether the product uploaded what it displayed; a difference is recorded with both texts rather than resolved by repeating the capture.

A host byte inspection of the exported bundle, of `train.jsonl` and `holdout.jsonl` and of the export manifest is the record of what left the product; a denied, expired or revoked trace or a secret-shaped string found there fails the run.

The trainer runs outside the product: its recorded exit status and the manifest it writes are the record of whether the exported corpus was accepted, and a corpus carrying a revoked trace must produce a non-zero exit rather than a completed run.

The base-versus-adapter comparison file the evaluator writes to the host, together with the archived Legion-Bench baseline it names, is the record of the evaluation result; the training run's own loss curve is not accepted as an evaluation.

A host listing of the bundle store after the recorded retention window, and a re-run of the exporter, are the record of whether the expired bundle was purged; the product's displayed retention state is not accepted on its own.
After each deletion a host listing shows the stored payload and its key absent, the receipt identifier matches what the product displayed, and a re-run of the exporter omits the deleted rows.
The consent, spool, export, retention and deletion state read directly from the host after each restart is the record; a state the product reports that the host contradicts fails the run.

recovery_cases.description: If the Stage 0 telemetry and training matrix has not been published, so the model revision, tokenizer, hyperparameters, seed, device, retention window and reproducibility threshold this run must use do not exist, the corpus, training, evaluation and retention legs are recorded blocked with that exact missing prerequisite named, never passed and never skipped; no substitute model, shorter run, different runtime or reduced hardware is used in their place.

If no host carrying the ratified model, runtime and hardware for the consent-gated adapter run is available, the training and evaluation legs are recorded blocked with that exact missing prerequisite; a dry run, a fixture smoke run or a recorded stand-in is never recorded as a training or evaluation result.

If the packaged product will only upload to a destination that cannot be pointed at a host-controlled endpoint, the upload, retry and revocation legs are recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite, namely the named external destination and its credential, and no third-party destination is contacted to complete them.

On the macOS and Linux cells, if no macOS host and Linux host with the packaged native product installed and a real display session, able to run the windowed GUI e2e suite, is available, that cell is recorded blocked with that exact prerequisite; a Windows result is never substituted for it.

A consent, preview, export, retention or deletion control the requirement names that the packaged build does not expose records the run failed with the exact missing control named; it is never recorded as passed against a partial control set and never recorded as skipped.

A trace whose consent was denied, expired or revoked that appears in an upload, in the exported bundle or in the exporter output fails the run as a privacy defect with the trace identifier and the host path named, and the export is destroyed.

A trainer or exporter run that completes against a corpus carrying a revoked trace is recorded as a defect with the trace named; the consent filter is not widened and the corpus is not edited during the run.

A repeated training run whose adapter hash or metrics fall outside the reproducibility threshold recorded before the first run is a valid failed result; the threshold is not moved after the result is observed.

A consent, spool, export, retention or deletion state the product reports after a restart that the host state contradicts fails the run, with both readings recorded and neither corrected during the run.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The collection endpoint is host-controlled and run-local; no third-party destination is contacted. The project is a disposable clone containing only synthetic content. Capture the consent state files, the previews, the endpoint log, the received payloads, the exported bundle and manifest, the corpus files, the trainer and evaluator manifests and exit statuses, the adapter hash and the deletion receipts. No model weights and no private raw trace are retained. Every received payload and every exported corpus file is inspected byte by byte before retention; one found to contain editor text, a prompt or a secret-shaped string outside the consented and previewed scope is destroyed and the run recorded as failed. Redact absolute user-home segments and any credential or endpoint token. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate and honour every deletion receipt.

steps: Install the separately labelled Manual/offline artifact for this configuration cell on a machine with no prior Legion state, record its SHA-256, and record the flavour its descriptor declares.
Start an OS-level per-process DNS, TCP and UDP capture over the artifact's whole process tree before the product is launched, and record the capture command and its start time.
Launch the product, complete first run, and record every consent control it exposes together with the state each starts in.
Grant crash, product and raw-training consent in full, which is the state in which an ordinary build would upload, and record the destination the product displays for each.

Work in a real project for the Manual/offline qualification period recorded for this run: open, edit, save, search, use Git and the local tooling, and produce training candidates through ordinary consented work.
Export the consented training bundle through the product's own export route to a host path and record the export, its manifest and their SHA-256 values.
Delete one exported bundle through the product, record the deletion receipt, and read the store back from the host.
Restart the product, then kill the process mid-work and restart it again, recording the consent, spool, export and deletion state after each restart.
Stop the capture, read it in full from the host, and record every destination it contains with the process that contacted it.

external_oracles.description: The OS-level per-process DNS, TCP and UDP capture, read from the host, is the record of every destination the artifact's process tree contacted for the whole run, including while every consent was granted; loopback counts only for a local server the run record names in advance.

A host listing of the spool, bundle and export directories after the run is the record that consented data stayed on the machine; a spool that drains with no destination in the capture is inspected rather than assumed delivered.
A host byte inspection of the exported bundle and its manifest is the record of what the export contains; a trace whose consent was denied or revoked, or a secret-shaped string, fails the run.
After the deletion a host listing shows the stored bundle and its key absent and the receipt identifier matches what the product displayed.
The consent, spool, export and deletion state read directly from the host after each restart and after the kill is the record; a state the product reports that the host contradicts fails the run.

The installed artifact SHA-256 and the flavour recorded in its descriptor are read from the host and matched against the candidate manifest for this configuration; an ordinary build is not accepted as the Manual/offline artifact.

recovery_cases.description: Any external destination in the capture fails the run and is recorded as a privacy defect with the destination and the contacting process named; the capture is not filtered and no destination is excluded to make the run pass.

Any fall back to a consented upload route, observed in the capture or in the spool, fails the run and is recorded with the exact route named; the consent state is not changed during the run to avoid it.

If no separately labelled Manual/offline artifact exists for this configuration cell, the run is recorded blocked with that exact missing prerequisite; an ordinary build with networking disabled by the host is never substituted for it.

If no OS-level per-process DNS, TCP and UDP capture is available on this cell, the run is recorded blocked with that exact missing prerequisite; the product's own report of its network activity is never accepted in its place.

On the macOS and Linux cells, if no macOS host and Linux host with the packaged native product installed and a real display session, able to run the windowed GUI e2e suite, is available, that cell is recorded blocked with that exact prerequisite; a Windows result is never substituted for it.
A consent, export or deletion control the requirement names that the Manual/offline build does not expose records the run failed with the exact missing control named, never passed and never skipped.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The machine has no prior Legion state and the project is a disposable clone containing only synthetic content. Capture the artifact hash and descriptor flavour, the consent states, the full network capture, the spool and export listings, the exported bundle and manifest, and the deletion receipts. The network capture is retained in full and is never edited; only host-identifying fields are reduced to a run-local pseudonym. The exported bundle is inspected byte by byte before retention and destroyed if it contains a secret-shaped string or an unconsented trace. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate and honour every deletion receipt.
